title: Decompose Engine F3 from the approved capability ledger
description:
Turn the approved capability membership for engine:F3 (Active-effect, concentration, and owned-entity lifecycle) into a
concrete implementation plan. This is real work, not a placeholder: decomposition
is what converts a hook-family label into implementable units, and doing it from
the ledger rather than from hook counts is the whole point.

Required output:

  * The GENERATED membership query for engine:F3 and its current result. Never a
    hand-copied count.
  * Every member clause classified into a REUSABLE IMPLEMENTATION PRIMITIVE.
    Organize children by primitive and by executable scenario, never by hook
    count and never one-child-per-clause.
  * Cross-family primitives named explicitly with their owning family, so the
    same primitive is not implemented twice under two epics.
  * The proposed implementation children, each naming (a) its conformance
    scenario and (b) the pack clauses it must actually execute.
  * Its PAIRED pack-projection bead(s) under eshyra-o9bd.19.3/.19.4 — projection
    and reference implementation are co-designed, so each proposed child names
    its projection counterpart.
  * Every boundary hint in the parent epic's description confirmed against the
    ledger rather than assumed. The hints are provisional.

Do NOT create implementation children before this bead closes.

COUNT HYGIENE: every number here is a SNAPSHOT. The generated ledger/predicate
is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a hand-copied number (e.g.
391, 399, 77, 79).

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX. engine:F1..F10 are the pack's
executionReadiness engineHooks families — NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
different F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit findings.
acceptance_criteria:
• A committed, runnable membership query for engine:F3, with its result recorded as a snapshot only.
• Every member clause mapped to a named reusable primitive.
• Proposed children listed with conformance scenario, pack clauses, and paired projection bead.
• Cross-family primitives resolved to a single owner.
• Parent-epic boundary hints confirmed or corrected against the ledger.
